title: [WA-036] Implement end-to-end mocked MVP test
description:
# Goal

Create an end-to-end test proving the MVP workflow.

## Test scenario

With mocked Telegram/weather/model provider:

1. Authorized user sends:
   "Dodaj Chwarzno jako lokalizację 54.4871, 18.4202"
2. User asks:
   "jaka będzie pogoda w Chwarznie w weekend?"
3. Bot resolves location/time and returns forecast summary.
4. User says:
   "jeśli porywy wiatru w weekend będą powyżej 12 m/s, powiadom mnie"
5. LLM proposes CEL:
   `max("wind_gusts_10m_ms", weekend()) >= 12`
6. User confirms.
7. Worker evaluates mocked forecast.
8. Notification candidate is generated.
9. Telegram sender sends a message containing `#R...` and `#E...`.
10. User asks:
   "dlaczego dostałem #E....?"
11. Bot explains based on persisted evaluation data.

## Acceptance criteria

- E2E test passes without real Telegram, weather API, or LLM calls.
- All external services are mocked.
- The test exercises DB persistence.
- The explanation is generated from stored event/evaluation data.

title: [WA-027] Implement LangGraph rule creation/edit confirmation flow
description:
# Goal

Allow the user to create and edit notification rules in natural Polish.

## Supported examples

- "w każdy piątek wyślij mi podsumowanie prognozy na weekend"
- "jeśli będzie padać, wyślij 15 minut przed"
- "jeśli nad Jeziorakiem średni wiatr będzie powyżej 7 m/s, daj znać dzień wcześniej"
- "powiadom mnie o drastycznym pogorszeniu pogody"
- "dodaj temperaturę do #R7K2"

## Rules

- LLM may emit a raw CEL expression.
- Bot must show the expression and human-readable explanation.
- User must confirm before activation.
- "Anomaly" or "drastic deterioration" is not special-cased; it is just a proposed CEL expression.
- After confirmation, runtime evaluation is deterministic and does not use LLM.

## Requirements

- Inject CEL function/metric allowlist into model context.
- Reject expressions with unknown functions/metrics.
- Store pending confirmations per Telegram context.
- Support editing existing rules by short ID.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tests cover successful proposal, validation failure, and user confirmation.
- Saved rules contain validated CEL.
- The model prompt/context includes available CEL functions and metrics.
- Ambiguous destructive edits ask for clarification.

title: [WA-018] Implement deduplication, cooldown and snooze
description:
# Goal

Prevent alert spam.

## Requirements

Implement:

- dedupe key
- cooldown per rule
- cooldown per location/phenomenon if useful
- snooze until timestamp
- last sent payload hash
- "significant change" threshold placeholder

## Suggested dedupe key

```text
rule_id + location_id + phenomenon_or_expression_hash + forecast_window_start + forecast_window_end
```

## Behavior

- If a similar alert was already sent for the same forecast window, suppress duplicates.
- If a user snoozes a rule, no notifications for that rule until snooze expires.
- Dry-run events should not be sent but should still show whether dedupe would suppress them.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tests cover duplicate suppression.
- Tests cover cooldown expiry.
- Tests cover snooze.

title: [WA-015] Integrate CEL expression engine and whitelisted functions
description:
# Goal

Integrate CEL for deterministic weather rule evaluation.

## Requirements

- Do not use Python `eval` or `exec`.
- Use a CEL implementation available for Python or isolate a CEL runtime if needed.
- Build a wrapper that:
  - validates syntax
  - validates allowed variables/functions
  - evaluates expressions against weather data
  - returns typed evaluation results
  - provides useful validation errors for the user

## Function allowlist exposed to the Foundation Model

The Foundation Model must receive this list in prompt/tool context when asked to propose CEL expressions.

### Time range helpers

- `now()`
- `today()`
- `tomorrow()`
- `weekend()`
- `next_hours(n)`
- `date_range(start_iso, end_iso)`
- `between(range, start_hhmm, end_hhmm)`
- `minutes(n)`
- `hours(n)`
- `previous_snapshot()`

### Aggregation/statistical helpers

- `min(metric, range)`
- `max(metric, range)`
- `avg(metric, range)`
- `sum(metric, range)`
- `median(metric, range)`
- `stddev(metric, range)`
- `pctl(metric, range, percentile)`

### Change/trend helpers

- `delta(metric, range)`
- `abs_delta(metric, range)`
- `rate_of_change(metric, range)`
- `forecast_delta(metric, range, previous_snapshot_ref)`

### Condition-over-time helpers

- `duration_where(condition, range)`
- `count_where(condition, range)`
- `any(condition, range)`
- `all(condition, range)`

### Numeric helpers

- `abs(x)`
- `round(x, digits)`
- `clamp(x, min_value, max_value)`

## Available metrics

At minimum:

- `temperature_2m_c`
- `apparent_temperature_c`
- `precipitation_mm`
- `precipitation_probability_pct`
- `rain_mm`
- `snowfall_cm`
- `cloud_cover_pct`
- `wind_speed_10m_ms`
- `wind_gusts_10m_ms`
- `wind_direction_10m_deg`
- `pressure_msl_hpa`
- `relative_humidity_2m_pct`
- `weather_code`

## Example expressions

```cel
max("wind_gusts_10m_ms", weekend()) >= 12
```

```cel
avg("wind_speed_10m_ms", next_hours(24)) >= 7
```

```cel
forecast_delta("apparent_temperature_c", tomorrow(), previous_snapshot()) <= -7
```

```cel
duration_where(precipitation_mm > 0.2, next_hours(12)) >= minutes(60)
```

## Acceptance criteria

- CEL syntax validation works before saving rules.
- Unknown function/metric names are rejected.
- Unit tests cover each helper category.
- The full function/metric list is available as a serializable object for prompts.
- Evaluator does not call the LLM.

title: [WA-009] Define Weather Provider contracts and normalized weather model
description:
# Goal

Define the weather provider abstraction and normalized data contracts.

## Provider interfaces

Create three provider protocols/interfaces:

```python
class ForecastProvider(Protocol):
    async def get_forecast(
        self,
        location: LocationRef,
        time_range: TimeRange,
        variables: list[WeatherVariable],
        resolution: ForecastResolution,
    ) -> ForecastResult: ...
```

```python
class ObservationProvider(Protocol):
    async def get_observations(
        self,
        location: LocationRef,
        radius_km: float,
        variables: list[WeatherVariable],
    ) -> ObservationResult: ...
```

```python
class WarningProvider(Protocol):
    async def get_warnings(
        self,
        location: LocationRef,
        time_range: TimeRange,
    ) -> list[WeatherWarning]: ...
```

## Required model types

Implement Pydantic/domain models:

```python
class LocationRef(BaseModel):
    id: str
    name: str
    latitude: float
    longitude: float
```

```python
class TimeRange(BaseModel):
    start: datetime
    end: datetime
    timezone: Literal["Europe/Warsaw"] = "Europe/Warsaw"
```

```python
class ForecastPoint(BaseModel):
    target_time: datetime
    fetched_at: datetime
    provider: str
    model: str | None
    location_id: str

    temperature_2m_c: float | None = None
    apparent_temperature_c: float | None = None
    precipitation_mm: float | None = None
    precipitation_probability_pct: float | None = None
    rain_mm: float | None = None
    snowfall_cm: float | None = None
    cloud_cover_pct: float | None = None
    wind_speed_10m_ms: float | None = None
    wind_gusts_10m_ms: float | None = None
    wind_direction_10m_deg: float | None = None
    pressure_msl_hpa: float | None = None
    relative_humidity_2m_pct: float | None = None
    weather_code: str | None = None

    raw_payload: dict
```

```python
class ForecastResult(BaseModel):
    provider: str
    model: str | None
    location: LocationRef
    fetched_at: datetime
    points: list[ForecastPoint]
    raw_payload: dict
```

```python
class ObservationPoint(BaseModel):
    observed_at: datetime
    fetched_at: datetime
    provider: str
    station_id: str | None
    station_name: str | None
    distance_km: float | None

    temperature_c: float | None = None
    wind_speed_ms: float | None = None
    wind_direction_deg: float | None = None
    pressure_hpa: float | None = None
    humidity_pct: float | None = None
    precipitation_mm: float | None = None

    raw_payload: dict
```

```python
class WeatherWarning(BaseModel):
    provider: str
    external_id: str
    location_id: str
    severity: str | None
    category: str
    headline: str
    description: str
    valid_from: datetime
    valid_to: datetime
    raw_payload: dict
```

## Design requirements

- All normalized field names must include units where ambiguity exists.
- Preserve raw provider payloads.
- Missing fields are represented as `None`, not fake values.
- Provider-specific weather codes must be mapped into a documented normalized code where practical.
- Provider failures must return typed errors and never cause fabricated weather data.

## Acceptance criteria

- Provider interfaces are independent from Telegram, LangGraph, and DB persistence.
- Unit tests validate model serialization.
- Docs explain how to add OpenWeather, AccuWeather, or meteo.pl later.

title: [WA-008] Implement DateResolver for Polish natural time ranges
description:
# Goal

Implement deterministic resolution of Polish natural time ranges.

## Scope

Support:

- `dziś`
- `dziś wieczorem`
- `jutro`
- `jutro rano`
- `jutro po południu`
- `jutro wieczorem`
- `następne 3 dni`
- `weekend`
- `ten weekend`
- `następny weekend`
- `majówka`
- explicit date ranges

## Rules

Timezone is always `Europe/Warsaw`.

Suggested mappings:

- `dziś`: now to 23:59
- `dziś wieczorem`: today 18:00-23:00
- `jutro`: tomorrow 00:00-23:59
- `jutro rano`: tomorrow 06:00-10:00
- `jutro po południu`: tomorrow 12:00-18:00
- `jutro wieczorem`: tomorrow 18:00-23:00
- `następne 3 dni`: now to now + 72h
- `weekend`: nearest upcoming Saturday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59
- `majówka`: range around May 1 and May 3 for the relevant year, including adjacent weekend/bridge days if configured

## Holiday data

Use a public holiday provider abstraction. First implementation should use Nager.Date with local DB cache. The resolver must still work from cache when the API is temporarily unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- Deterministic unit tests with frozen clock.
- Tests cover edge cases around Friday/Saturday/Sunday.
- Tests cover "majówka" for at least two years.
- DateResolver returns explicit start/end datetimes and a human-readable explanation.

title: Telegram Weather AI Agent — LangGraph/LangSmith learning project
description:
# Epic: Telegram Weather AI Agent

Build a self-hosted Telegram weather AI agent for Polish-language usage.

## Product goal

The bot must:
- answer Polish natural-language weather questions,
- manage multiple named locations,
- create/edit/delete/snooze weather notification rules,
- evaluate scheduled and event-based notifications deterministically,
- send official IMGW alerts and current synoptic data,
- preserve conversation context per Telegram thread/topic,
- be deployed on a homelab via Docker Compose,
- use LangGraph/LangChain/LangSmith heavily as a learning objective.

## Key architecture decisions

- Telegram remains the user interface.
- Use Telegram private supergroup + Topics for threaded context.
- Context key: `chat_id + message_thread_id`; fallback to `chat_id`.
- Foundation model default: `gpt-5-mini`, configurable through LangChain.
- Supported language: Polish only.
- Supported timezone: `Europe/Warsaw` only for now.
- Units are global, not per location.
- Weather forecast source for MVP: Open-Meteo DWD ICON.
- Current observations: IMGW synop endpoint.
- Official warnings: IMGW meteorological/hydrological warnings.
- Holidays: public holiday API + local cache, preferably Nager.Date.
- Persistence: PostgreSQL + TimescaleDB.
- Rule expressions: CEL + whitelisted weather/statistical helper functions.
- LLM may propose raw CEL expressions, but user must confirm before activation.
- Anomalies are not special-cased; they are normal CEL-based rules.
- Rule evaluation must never depend on the LLM at runtime.
- Observability: LangSmith for LLM/LangGraph traces within free/low-cost limits; structured logs and DB audit for durable self-hosted observability.

## Global units

```yaml
temperature: celsius
wind_speed: m/s
precipitation: mm
pressure: hPa
```

## Definition of done for the Epic

The Epic is complete when:
- a user can run the system with `docker compose up`,
- the bot answers weather questions for named locations,
- the bot supports Telegram authorization,
- the bot supports location CRUD and global units,
- the bot resolves Polish natural time ranges like "jutro", "weekend", "majówka",
- the bot can create, edit, disable, delete, snooze, and explain rules,
- rules are evaluated via CEL using persisted weather snapshots,
- notifications contain short IDs for rules/events,
- Open-Meteo DWD ICON forecasts are fetched and persisted,
- IMGW warnings and synop observations are fetched and surfaced,
- LangGraph is used for the conversational workflow,
- LangSmith traces/evals are wired for learning,
- task-level tests and at least one end-to-end dry run pass.

title: [WA-002] Create architecture ADRs and domain vocabulary
description:
# Goal

Document the key architecture decisions so later agents can work in fresh contexts without rediscovering the project shape.

## Required ADRs

Create ADR files under `docs/adr/`:

1. Telegram as UI; private supergroup + Topics for threaded contexts.
2. LangGraph/LangChain/LangSmith as learning-first orchestration stack.
3. PostgreSQL + TimescaleDB for relational + time-series persistence.
4. CEL + whitelisted helper functions instead of Python eval.
5. Weather provider abstraction split into Forecast/Observation/Warning providers.
6. Deterministic rule evaluation; LLM only proposes or edits rules.
7. Docker Compose as initial homelab deployment target.
8. Global units and Poland-only timezone/language scope.

## Domain vocabulary

Create `docs/domain-vocabulary.md` defining:

- authorized user
- location
- global units
- forecast
- forecast snapshot
- observation
- official warning
- rule
- rule expression
- rule ID
- event ID
- notification
- cooldown
- dedupe key
- snooze
- Telegram context key
- dry run

## Acceptance criteria

- ADRs are concise but explicit.
- Each ADR includes context, decision, consequences.
- The vocabulary is referenced from README or AGENTS.md.
